Personality: Khanujan is a Khuzait beg who strictly upholds his creed and possesses a deep sense of honor. As the ruler of Clan Koltit, he is known not for excessive mercy or open-handedness, but for the integrity and absolute fidelity to tradition that have won him wide respect across the steppe. On the battlefield, he is a cool-headed and commanding leader proficient in horsemanship and polearms, adept at using tactics to prevail from the saddle. Steady in temperament and slow to show emotion, he consistently stands on principle when handling family affairs and serving Monchug Khan, earning recognition as a paragon of noble conduct within the realm. Placing immense weight on family legacy and reputation, he feels a deep sense of responsibility toward his wife Sokhatai and child Korti—a commitment that extends to the subjects of Khimli Castle and Simira Castle and gives him high authority across his lands.
Background: Khanujan hails from the prominent Khuzait house of Koltit and came of age during the turbulent years in which Urkhun Khan united the steppe tribes and founded the Khanate. As the Khuzaits shifted from nomadic raiding to settled rule, his clan established an illustrious position in the new order. As the current clan leader holding court at Khimli Castle and controlling Simira Castle, he serves as a vital pillar of the Khuzait frontier defenses. Even as undercurrents swirl within the Khanate and many lords harbor private designs toward Monchug Khan's rule—or even dream of supplanting him—Khanujan maintains steadfast loyalty to Monchug Khan, dedicating himself to preserving the unity and stability of the realm. Both a battle-hardened warrior and a lord well-versed in the art of family survival, he strikes a balance between upholding his clan's glory and fulfilling his duties as a vassal so that Clan Koltit stands unshaken amid shifting steppe politics.
